title: VITA: Vision-to-Action Flow Matching Policy
claim: Conventional generative policies start from noise and repeatedly inject conditions; ours flows directly from input representations to outputs, removing noise and conditioning modules.
layout: 2 panels split by vertical dashed line, left-to-right flow in each, conventional on left and ours on right, distribution heatmaps above or beside boxes
description: A two-panel comparison separated by a vertical dashed line. The left panel, 'Conventional Flow Matching Policy', has two rows. The top row runs from a robot camera image to a 'Latent Image' box to an 'Inject Conditions' label with three downward arrows. The bottom row runs from a Gaussian heatmap to a 'Noise' box, then into three teal-to-green wavy flow arrows labelled 'Flow Matching', ending at a trajectory of colored dots labelled 'Actions'. The right panel, 'VITA Policy: Noise-Free Flow Matching', is a single straight path. A camera image feeds a 'Latent Image' box, which connects by wavy flow arrows to a 'Latent Actions' box and then to the action trajectory. Blue-pink heatmaps above the two latent boxes show the latent image and latent action distributions, linked by dashed arrows. The muted blue-gray boxes and the teal flow arrows are the main visual elements.
caption: A comparison between \ABBR and conventional flow matching and diffusion policies. Unlike conventional methods that sample noise from standard distributions and inject input modalities via conditioning, \ABBR poses no constraints on the source distribution, and flows directly from latent visual representations to latent actions, eliminating the need for conditioning modules.
abstract: Conventional flow matching and diffusion-based policies sample via iterative denoising from standard noise distributions (e.g., Gaussian), and require conditioning modules to repeatedly incorporate visual information during the generative process, incurring substantial time and memory overhead. To reduce the complexity, we develop VITA (Vision-To-Action flow matching policy), a noise-free and conditioning-free flow matching policy learning framework that directly flows from visual representations to latent actions. Since the source of the flow is visually grounded, VITA eliminates the need for visual conditioning during generation. As expected, bridging vision and action is challenging, because actions are lower-dimensional, less structured, and sparser than visual representations; moreover, flow matching requires the source and target to have the same dimensionality. To overcome this, we introduce an action autoencoder that maps raw actions into a structured latent space aligned with visual latents, trained jointly with flow matching. To further prevent latent action space collapse during end-to-end training, we propose flow latent decoding, which anchors the latent generation process by backpropagating the action reconstruction loss through the flow matching ODE (ordinary differential equation) solving steps. We evaluate VITA on 9 simulation and 5 real-world tasks from ALOHA and Robomimic. VITA achieves 1.9x faster inference compared to conventional flow matching with conditioning modules, while outperforming or matching state-of-the-art policies. Project page: https://ucd-dare.github.io/VITA/.
